Summary: Compact multi-team delivery for small local UI, API, console, or library applications.
ValueStatement: A single implementation owner builds the requested application while independent QA proves the acceptance contract and a delivery manager contains unresolved outcomes.
InterfaceContractSummary: Project structure and launch variables define the application profile, product root, acceptance criteria, and proof appropriate to the application kind.
ManagerOverrideSummary: The manager may classify unsupported risk or close an unresolved repair with a bounded follow-up decision, but may not waive missing acceptance proof.
GovernanceNotes: This lane is intentionally limited to small local applications. Production deployment, privileged operations, regulated data, payments, destructive migrations, and unresolved security boundaries require a specialist process.
ChangeSummary: Adds a compact framework-neutral multi-team lane with one mutation owner, independent validation, one bounded repair, and manager-contained terminal paths.
GovernancePolicySummary: Require only proof applicable to the declared application kind; do not impose browser or runtime gates on console and library work.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Agents own implementation and validation within the approved product root. Reviewers do not mutate concurrently with the implementation owner.
OperatingModeSummary: Governed local development with bounded repair and no deployment execution.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Suitable for bounded, low-risk application, service, tool, and library delivery.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Resolve the delivery contract, keep scope bounded, and close normal or exceptional paths.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Use an agent with project-structure, process-artifact, and delivery decision readiness.
RoleUsages.Notes: Owns process decisions but does not perform implementation work.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Review the application profile, product boundary, and unsupported-risk classification.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Use an agent able to review multiple application kinds without introducing framework assumptions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Reviews the contract and architecture; remains read-only during implementation.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Scaffold when necessary, implement the complete acceptance contract, and repair validation findings.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Use an agent with workspace mutation, scaffolding, build, test, and local runtime readiness for the selected stack.
RoleUsages.Notes: The only role authorized to mutate the product target.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Independently validate build, tests, runtime behavior, and acceptance proof appropriate to the application kind.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Use an agent with read-only product access and the validation tools required by the application profile.
RoleUsages.Notes: Validates independently and routes concrete findings to the repair owner.

Steps.Title: Resolve simple application contract
Steps.Subtitle: Kind, root, criteria, proof, and risk
Steps.Notes: Produce a typed application profile before implementation. Choose exactly one supported kind and one risk disposition.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use project-structure source-of-truth data and explicit launch constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Define application kind, stack, product root, entry point, acceptance criteria, applicable proof, exclusions, and risk disposition.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Cite the project/node identifiers and managed contract artifact.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The manager owns classification; the architect reviews boundary and risk.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select specialist-review-required only for a named unsupported-risk trigger; ambiguity alone is resolved conservatively in the contract.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to a delivery-capable agent with project-structure access.
Rebind to a framework-neutral architecture reviewer.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application delivery contract
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, QA, repair, and handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must declare applicationKind as UI, WebApi, Console, or Library; technology stack; approved product root; entry project or command; acceptance criteria; applicable build, test, runtime, HTTP, browser, console, or consumer proof; and riskDisposition as SimpleSupported or SpecialistReviewRequired with a typed reason.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Simple delivery supported
BranchOutcomes.Description: The work is local, bounded, and eligible for autonomous implementation.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Specialist review required
BranchOutcomes.Description: A typed deployment, privilege, security, data, payment, migration, or production-infrastructure risk is outside this lane.

Steps.Title: Implement simple application
Steps.Subtitle: Single mutation owner
Steps.Notes: Scaffold if required, then implement every acceptance criterion in the approved product root. Scaffolding is not a completed deliverable.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the accepted simple application contract.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce the complete product change set and a criterion-by-criterion self-review.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Record changed files and current build, test, or smoke receipts appropriate to the stack.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The implementation owner is the only product mutator.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only on a concrete tool, access, policy, or environment failure with a failed receipt.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an agent with mutation and validation readiness for the selected stack.
Reviewer remains read-only while the implementation owner is active.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by QA, repair, and handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must list created and changed files, scaffold command when used, entry project or command, acceptance-criteria mapping, validation receipts, and known risks.

Steps.Title: Independently validate application
Steps.Subtitle: Profile-specific build, test, and behavior proof
Steps.Notes: Validate the approved product root without mutation and select exactly one branch.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the contract and implementation change set.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce independent proof and either accept quality or identify bounded repair findings.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Use only proof applicable to the declared application kind and cite current-run receipts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA owns the validation verdict; implementation evidence is input, not acceptance.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Route product defects and proof gaps to repair-required. Block only when a concrete failure prevents a branch decision.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an independent validator with the profile-required tools.
The reviewer may clarify the contract but may not replace QA proof.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application validation evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by repair and final handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include current build and test results plus profile-specific evidence: UI browser behavior and console status, WebApi HTTP assertions, Console invocation with output and exit code, or Library tests and consumer-facing contract proof.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Quality accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: All acceptance criteria have current applicable proof.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Repair required
BranchOutcomes.Description: Concrete product defects or proof gaps can be repaired within the approved scope.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Require a current build only when the selected stack declares the .NET build tool.
Require a current test run only when the selected stack declares the .NET test tool.
Require local runtime startup only when the application profile declares it.
Require browser proof only for profiles that declare a browser-visible surface.

Steps.Title: Repair validation findings
Steps.Subtitle: One bounded repair
Steps.Notes: Repair only the findings from independent validation, then run the smallest relevant checks.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the contract and concrete QA findings.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce a bounded repair change set mapped to every finding.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Cite changed files and targeted check receipts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The same implementation owner performs the only repair mutation cycle.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not expand scope; record findings that cannot be repaired for manager resolution.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Retain the implementation owner when possible; otherwise rebind with the full QA evidence.
QA remains read-only and does not pre-accept the repair.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by revalidation and repaired handoff.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must map every QA finding to cause, changed files, targeted checks, and disposition.

Steps.Title: Revalidate repaired application
Steps.Subtitle: Fresh independent proof
Steps.Notes: Repeat the applicable acceptance proof against the repaired product root and select exactly one branch.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the original contract, QA findings, and repair change set.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce fresh proof and either accept the repaired application or route unresolved findings to the manager.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Do not reuse stale pre-repair success receipts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Independent QA owns the repaired verdict.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Any remaining defect, proof gap, or concrete environment blocker routes to manager-resolution-required.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an independent validator with the profile-required tools.
The manager receives unresolved evidence but may not waive it.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Repaired application validation evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by repaired handoff or manager resolution.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must contain fresh profile-specific build, test, runtime, behavior, cleanup, and remaining-finding evidence.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Quality accepted after repair
BranchOutcomes.Description: Fresh proof satisfies every acceptance criterion.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Manager resolution required
BranchOutcomes.Description: A bounded repair was attempted and unresolved evidence requires a managed decision.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Require a fresh build only when the selected stack declares the .NET build tool.
Require a fresh test run only when the selected stack declares the .NET test tool.
Require fresh runtime startup only when the application profile declares it.
Require fresh browser proof only for profiles that declare a browser-visible surface.

Steps.Title: Handoff accepted application
Steps.Subtitle: Compact evidence index
Steps.Notes: Produce a concise final handoff from the accepted contract, change set, and QA proof.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce the final application path, run command, validation summary, and evidence index.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Reference existing receipts; do not rerun implementation or validation.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The manager closes only the accepted branch.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not invent missing proof or convert open defects into acceptance.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to a delivery manager with access to the accepted evidence.
QA confirms the handoff cites the accepted evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application handoff
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for project writeback, documentation, and future maintenance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must list product root, entry project or command, implemented criteria, build and test status, profile-specific runtime proof, cleanup status, known limitations, and evidence references.

Steps.Title: Handoff repaired application
Steps.Subtitle: Compact repaired evidence index
Steps.Notes: Produce a concise final handoff from the accepted repaired branch.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Produce the final application path, repaired findings, run command, validation summary, and evidence index.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Reference both the repair and fresh QA receipts.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The manager closes only the accepted repaired branch.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not accept unresolved revalidation findings.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to a delivery manager with access to the repair and accepted revalidation evidence.
QA confirms the handoff cites fresh accepted evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Repaired simple application handoff
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for project writeback, documentation, and future maintenance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must list product root, entry project or command, repaired findings, implemented criteria, fresh build and test status, profile-specific runtime proof, cleanup status, known limitations, and evidence references.

Steps.Title: Resolve persistent findings
Steps.Subtitle: Manager-contained terminal decision
Steps.Notes: Close the bounded lane with a concrete disposition; do not ask an operator to code or fabricate acceptance.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the contract, repair change set, and fresh unresolved QA evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Choose a typed disposition: FollowUpRepair, ReplanScope, EnvironmentAction, or UnsupportedRiskProcess.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Name the exact unresolved findings, owner, next process, and preserved evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The manager may contain and route the issue but may not mark quality accepted.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: This is a terminal managed outcome, not an operator escalation or a second unbounded repair loop.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Keep the decision with a delivery manager able to route a bounded next action.
Implementation owner explains technical repair implications without mutating.
QA preserves the unresolved evidence and prevents false acceptance.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application unresolved decision
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable to launch a focused repair or specialist process.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must contain a typed disposition, unresolved finding ids, preserved evidence, accountable owner, bounded next scope, and an explicit statement that quality was not accepted.

Steps.Title: Route unsupported application risk
Steps.Subtitle: Specialist process decision
Steps.Notes: Close this lane with a typed specialist routing decision before any product mutation occurs.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Use the typed unsupported-risk classification from the application contract.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Name the specialist process or prerequisite that must own the work.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Preserve the trigger, affected criteria, and accountable routing owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The manager routes the work and this lane performs no implementation.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not downgrade the typed risk merely to keep the simple lane moving.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Keep routing accountable to the delivery manager.
The architect confirms the unsupported-risk trigger and specialist boundary.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Simple application risk routing decision
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable as intake for the selected specialist process.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must contain the typed unsupported-risk trigger, affected scope, specialist process or prerequisite, accountable owner, and confirmation that no product mutation occurred.
